The truly disgusting part of it is that the "budget" isn't a "budget" in the everyman sense of the word. If I set a budget, but don't end up spending all of it, I sock it away or use it for something else. When a government agency has excess budget, it HAS to spend it. No saving to require less budget next year, no fiscal responsibility at all. Spend, spend, spend.

It isn't so much that they have to spend the money, but they are strongly encouraged to because if your program doesn't spend it then next year you get that much less. So say you have a really good year and don't have to spend so much. If you don't find a way to spend it, then your budget is going to be short next year.

As an example let's take the programs that I work on. We do well, stay on top of maintenance and stuff doesn't break, requiring expensive replacements. So we spend x less than our budget this year, so next year we get that much less, then a multi-million dollar part fries and we have to replace it, but now we don't have the budget to do so. To prevent things like that from happening we have to spend out the budget at the end of each year. Trust me I would rather the excess funds go to paying off...well anything, but that isn't how the game is played.
Either way you slice it, the end result sucks. That's not how a rational or functional person runs an organization. It's a recipe for wasteful spending.
